sentences.text:
For Appellant : Mr.S.Sarvagan Prabhu  For R4 : Mr.M.E.Ilango  R3 : Died  For R1, 5 and 6 : No appearance  *****
 JUDGMENT
The Insurance Company has preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.
2.It is a case of fatal.
The contention of the Insurance Company is that the offending vehicle came on the wrong side, i.e., on the right side of the road instead of travelling on left side, therefore, the accident occurred.
The Tribunal has taken note of this fact but has recorded that the first respondent who had insured the vehicle with the appellant was driving the vehicle in a high speed.
Hence, based on the rash and negligent driving, the liability is fixed on the Insurance Company.
It is seen that the appellant vehicle was travelling in a Thanjavur Highway.
Generally, any vehicle in Highway ought to go in high speed.
Therefore, it cannot be stated that the vehicle had travelled in high speed.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Having held so, the vehicle ought to have driven with caution also,
hence liability is fixed on the vehicle 3.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that instead of fixing 50-50 liability on the vehicles, it would be fair to fix 70% liability on the vehicle which was travelling on the right side and the 30% liability on the vehicle which had travelled in high speed.
Therefore, this Court is modifying the above said ratio alone and other portion of the impugned order is confirmed.
Thus, this Court is fixing 70% liability on the 4th respondent herein and 30% liability on the appellant herein.

The total compensation granted by the Tribunal is Rs. 3,52,834/-.
4.

The appellant Insurance Company is directed to deposit Rs.1,05,850/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum and costs to the credit of M.C.O.P., on the file of claims Tribunal, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

The 4 th respondent Insurance Company is directed to deposit Rs.2,46,984/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum to the credit of M.C.O.P., on the file of claims Tribunal, less t h e a m o u n t a l r e a d y d e p o s i t e d , i f a n y , w i t h i n a p e r i o d o f e i g h t w e e k s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposits, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the same with accrued interests and costs, less the amount already withdrawn by them, if any, by filing appropriate application before the Tribunal.
